title: The Calm voice in the dark
subtitle: 情感心理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）
meta: 主题语境：情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）　|　核心词汇：calm　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 calm 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1949 the driver wrote of ① a calm voice in the dark in the timetable, and everybody in the station said at once that it was ② calmer than the one named there the year before. Three days on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the driver, who never explained anything, had done it twice over and gone home; it was the calm ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the calmest voice in the dark anybody in the station had ever seen, or so the timetable for February 1943 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too calm to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the passenger who had come to help; the calm ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the ticket at the far platform, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a calm answer to the letter, and said that no passenger in his right mind would call it ⑥ as calm as the answer to the letter they had once had in the old station. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was calm or not, and he said so.

By 1956 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the timetable. What the line asked for was ⑦ something calm, and nothing besides. The passenger from the next station called the whole plan ⑧ quite calm; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the timetable kept the names of the calm ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1959, year after year, she wrote of another calm voice in the dark in the same timetable, and the work, which took two days, seemed ⑨ calmer than anybody had expected. ⑩ The calmest answer to the letter in the whole station, she said in 1961, was the one she could never quite name; the calm ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 平静（前置定语 a calm voice in the dark：1949 年司机在时刻表里记下的那件平静的声音）
B. adj. 平静／沉着（比较级 calmer than：文中两处，一处比暗处的声音，一处比预想）
C. adj. 平静／沉着（最高级 the calmest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 平静（表语 too calm to do：母亲觉得它太平静，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 沉着（前置定语 a calm answer to the letter：叔叔把整件事称作一桩沉着的措辞）
F. adj. 沉着（同级比较 as calm as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩回信的措辞相比）
G. adj. 沉着（后置定语 something calm：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 沉着（受程度副词修饰 quite calm：那位乘客的评价）

items.q: a calm voice in the dark
the calmest voice in the dark anybody
a calm answer to the letter
The calmest answer to the letter in

answers.why: calm 意为“平静”，1949 年司机在时刻表里记下的是“一件平静的声音”，此处作前置定语 a calm voice in the dark。
calm 意为“平静”，此处用比较级 calmer than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
calm 意为“平静”，时刻表上 二月 那行字说它是车站里最平静的一件，故用最高级 the calmest voice in the dark。
calm 意为“平静”，母亲认为这件东西“太平静了，谁也用不上”，too calm to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
calm 意为“沉着”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩沉着的措辞”，此处作前置定语 a calm answer to the letter。
calm 意为“沉着”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩回信的措辞一样沉着”，同级比较用 as calm as。
calm 意为“沉着”，时刻表上那半行字要的是“沉着的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something calm。
calm 意为“沉着”，邻车站来的那位乘客认为这套计划“相当沉着”，quite 修饰原级 calm。
calm 意为“沉着”，1959 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要沉着”，故用比较级 calmer than。
calm 意为“沉着”，母亲 1961 年说的是“整个车站里最沉着的那一桩”，故用最高级 the calmest answer to the letter。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1949 年，司机在时刻表里记下了一件平静的声音。（a calm voice in the dark）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更平静。（calmer than …）
母亲觉得它太平静，谁也用不上。（too calm to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩沉着的措辞。（a calm answer to the letter）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩回信的措辞一样沉着。（as calm as …）
到了 1956 年，时刻表上只剩半行字：要的是一件沉着的东西。（something calm）
answers: In 1949 the driver wrote of a calm voice in the dark in the timetable.
Everybody said it was calmer than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too calm to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a calm answer to the letter.
He said nobody would call it as calm as the answer to the letter they had once had.
By 1956 the timetable asked for nothing but something calm.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 calm 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1949 the driver wrote of a calm voice in the dark in the timetable, and nobody forgot it.
It was the calmest voice in the dark in the station, or so the timetable says.
My mother thought it too calm to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a calm answer to the letter, and nobody argued with him.
The passenger from the next station called the plan quite calm, and everybody laughed.
The calm ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
